name: the Lunnet
identity: Cheerful marsh folk in stilt villages: ferry-keepers, reed-weavers and herbalists, famous for frog choirs and terrible puns.
architecture: Round reed-thatched houses on stilts, joined by plank walkways and little ferries, with a floating garden tied up outside every door.

festivals.name: the Frog Choir
festivals.description: The whole marsh sings back to the frogs. The frogs usually win.

festivals.name: the Firefly Ferry
festivals.description: Boats drift with gourd-lanterns while everyone takes a turn telling their very worst joke.

festivals.name: the Big Dry
festivals.description: When the water drops, the village hunts the mud for everything it lost during the year, and some things it did not.

values: never laughing at a joke too early
pride: Their ferries, which can find any channel in thick fog, and the fact that nobody has ever successfully invaded a marsh.

makersMarks: a little frog carved somewhere hard to find
a reed knot only the maker can tie

relations.note: Eel pie against meat-and-onion pie, judged every Haymoot, never settled.
Neighbors on the marsh-forest edge who share their lantern festivals.
Rush paper and dried herbs for Ochrel glass, by a very long caravan road.
